Because a plugin runs inside ATAK's process, you debug it like any Android app attached to ATAK, and you test it with standard Android tooling.

Debugging

  • Logcat. Use ATAK's logging (com.atakmap.coremap.log.Log) or Android's android.util.Log and filter logcat by your TAG. The example logs lifecycle transitions (onStart, onResume, …) and receiver activity — keep that habit; it makes the load/enable sequence visible.
  • Attach the debugger. Install the debug build (installCivDebug), launch ATAK, then Attach Debugger to Android Process in Android Studio and pick the ATAK process. Breakpoints in your plugin code work normally because your classes are loaded into that process.
  • Iterate. Re-run installCivDebug to push a new build; restart ATAK so it reloads the plugin.

Testing

The example ships both instrumentation and unit tests, which are a good model:

  • app/src/androidTest/… — instrumentation tests that run on a device/emulator with ATAK present (e.g. MapTest, GeocoordTest, and a HelloWorldRobot helper that drives the plugin UI).
  • app/src/test/… — local unit tests for logic that doesn't need the device.

Run them with the usual Gradle test tasks (matching your flavor), e.g. ./gradlew testCivDebugUnitTest for unit tests and ./gradlew connectedCivDebugAndroidTest for instrumentation tests on a connected device.

Common pitfalls

Symptom Likely cause
AlertDialog/Toast crashes instantly Built with the plugin context instead of getMapView().getContext().
Plugin never appears in ATAK API marker mismatch, or the com.atakmap.app.component discovery hook is missing/renamed inconsistently.
Resources not found (R.layout/R.drawable null) Inflated/loaded with the MapView context instead of the plugin context.
Works in debug, breaks in release ProGuard stripped/renamed classes referenced reflectively or via plugin.xml; add keep rules in proguard-gradle.txt.
Duplicate panels stack up Missing the isClosed() / unhideDropDown() re-open guard in onReceive.
Theme looks wrong context.setTheme(R.style.ATAKPluginTheme) not called in MapComponent.onCreate.
